title: Stratified build cache + deterministic base-image pipeline to cut CI critical-path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: CI critical-path latency remains a major source of developer friction and release slowdown. This ticket implements two coordinated efforts: (1) introduce a stratified cache model that separates stable base layers, language/toolchain layers, and ephemeral app artifact layers; and (2) a deterministic base-image build pipeline (signed, versioned) so we can reuse base artifacts across runners and speed up cache hits. Goals: reduce median CI job wall-time for hotpaths (unit-tests and integration smoke) by >=30%, shrink average image pull size, and make local dev builds more reproducible.
motivation_and_background: We see several recurring patterns: many jobs miss cache due to brittle Dockerfile ordering and timestamps; toolchain installs are repeated across many images; CI runners fetch large base images that change frequently; lint and typecheck steps still run in heavier images rather than in slim base nodes. Prior tickets improved cache priming but didn't introduce deterministic base-image builds or a clear cache stratification. This work complements ongoing toolchain unification and remote dep mounts.
acceptance_criteria: New stratified cache layout documented and enabled in >= 75% of CI workflows listed in the architecture doc
Deterministic base-image pipeline produces signed image artifact with content-hash tag and stored in the internal registry
Median wall-time for the canonical CI hotpath pipeline reduced by >= 30% on master branch compared to baseline (baseline measured 2025-10-15)
Cache hit-rate for base and toolchain layers increases to >= 85% across ephemeral CI runners
Migration guide and developer notes published, with rollback steps and opt-out flags
At least two representative repositories (webserver and inference-runtime) migrated and green for two consecutive cycles
Performance dashboards added to Console showing per-step duration and cache hit metrics
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: a deterministic build pipeline introduces new operational steps and may break consumers if tags are consumed incorrectly. Mitigation: produce both stable content-hash tags and legacy semver tags during rollout; add feature flag to opt-out per-repo; run canary on non-prod runners for two weeks. Risk: pushing signed images may increase registry storage. Mitigation: enable lifecycle rules and manifest deduplication, and schedule monthly pruning for staging artifacts.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype deterministic base-image build using buildkit reproducible flags and a canonical dockerfile in infra/repos/base-images. 2) Define stratified cache policy: base-layer (OS + common libs), toolchain-layer (language runtimes, package managers), app-layer (repo artifacts). 3) Implement cache keys and migration shims in CI config (GH Actions / internal runner), add remote cache attachments and lazy mounts for large deps. 4) Add signing step and publish manifest to internal registry with content-hash tag. 5) Migrate two pilot repos, measure metrics, and iterate. 6) Ramp to full org with rollout plan and rollback scripts.
implementation_notes: Prefer BuildKit with --export-cache and inline cache metadata. Use swhash/content digest to tag images. For npm/pip/cargo toolchains use prebuilt layer tarballs uploaded to the registry and mounted into ephemeral runners to avoid repeated installs. Lint/toolchain containers will be slimmed to a separate pool so CI lint jobs can run on smaller images. We will reuse the existing artifact signing KMS integration from private deploys.
testing_plan: Automated smoke pipeline to validate signed images; synthetic microbenchmarks to measure pull times and layer re-use; A/B comparison jobs (canary vs baseline) for 2 weeks; developer acceptance testing docs for local reproducible build steps.
measurement: Add metrics to Console: job_duration_ms, step_duration_ms (checkout, build, install), cache_hit_ratio by layer, image_pull_bytes, registry_storage_bytes. Baseline comparisons and weekly trend lines. Target: CI hotpath median time -30% and cache_hit_ratio >=85%.
migration_and_rollout: Pilot: webserver repo and inference-runtime repo for 2 weeks. If metrics pass, enable org-wide in opt-in mode then opt-out removed after 6 weeks. Provide migration checklist: update Dockerfile ordering, remove ephemeral apt-get layers, add BUILDSTAMP file, adopt content-hash tags.
